title: Prove exact sparse tensor-annihilator coefficient valuations (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove exact coefficient valuations for every minimum-term integer-power support of the fixed tensor generator `D=diag(1,(3+4i)/5)`. Claim type: scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. This answers the arithmetic-order part of Open next question 2 in merged [#5934](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5934).

For `n=f+1`, exponents `m_0<...<m_n` and positive integer gaps `delta_s`, the primitive Gaussian-integer relation has

```text
v_(2+i)(c_j) = sum_(s=j)^(n-1) (n-1-s) delta_s
v_(2-i)(c_j) = sum_(s=0)^(j-1) s delta_s

total valuation mass
  = sum_s [n-1+2s(n-1-s)] delta_s
  >= 2 binom(n+1,3), with equality exactly for consecutive supports.
```

Thus arbitrary nonconsecutive supports, including Laurent supports and arbitrarily high degree, cannot reduce the quadratic maximum coefficient bit height or cubic explicit coefficient-list storage order at the same `f+2` term count. The exact actual-modulus optimum remains open. No new kappa, physical supplier or selected-frontier change is claimed.

The new [proof](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/025e0a934635dbcd0e1321dba36decdd96235c9a/research/sparse-tensor-annihilator-heights/PROOF.md), verifier and [reproduction guide](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/025e0a934635dbcd0e1321dba36decdd96235c9a/research/sparse-tensor-annihilator-heights/README.md) are isolated under `research/sparse-tensor-annihilator-heights/`.

Credit Nick Petalas #5934 for the valuation method, consecutive-support theorem and explicit question; zxv [#5436](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5436) for the fixed-generator tensor escape and coefficient-pricing problem; Anthony Chefles for classical multi-copy independence; and the retained native/control lineage. Vandermonde and Gaussian-integer methods are classical. Predecessor results are cited premises; no predecessor scientific verifier was replayed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Evidence

- Before, #5934 determines only consecutive-power coefficient heights. After, the written theorem determines both split-prime valuations for every integer exponent support and proves the sharp weighted-gap mass minimum.
- The new census checks 246 supports, including 240 nonconsecutive ones, by signed Vandermonde cofactors and a separate exact rational kernel solver. It checks 1,190 coefficient occurrences, 944 root residuals and 1,776 literal lifted diagonal entries. The sample and rejection controls are additional to those census counts.
- Thirteen controls reject invalid supports, altered or missing coefficients, nonprimitive scaling, a zero coefficient and conjugated coefficients. All checks remain enabled under optimized Python.
- Both registered warning-strict commands pass on CPython 3.12.15 with identical generated six-file hash-bound receipts. They took 0.256 and 0.258 seconds locally, below their 60-second limits. These are check durations, not a performance comparison.
- Metadata/source pins, in-memory syntax compilation, whitespace, exact committed bytes/modes/source-history ancestry, official seven-member export integrity and input coverage pass. Both read-only Git-free exported replays with an empty executable PATH agree with the local receipt.

Exact commands from the repository root:


[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19541730). Canonical main was refreshed before submission and remains `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, priority revision 8. The selected #7000 binding control passed; no selected scientific replay was run. The card's scope change to this arithmetic side result and exact provenance are declared in TASK.json and SOURCES.json.

## Limitations

The theorem fixes the generator, exact equality, Gaussian-rational coefficient field and minimum term count. It optimizes split-prime valuation mass, not the full complex-modulus objective. More terms, approximate cancellation, other generators and factored or streaming descriptions are outside the claim. It supplies no productive physical consumer, coefficient-generation price, precision, field-pass, ownership/restoration, tape, compiler or outer invoice. The five selected framework assumptions remain. Selected cold replay, predecessor scientific suites, Lean and Docker are unrun and unclaimed. No registered mathematical command was deferred to CI.

## Open next questions

- Do consecutive supports minimize the actual maximum primitive coefficient modulus? Start at f=2 by controlling the extra Gaussian prime factors of the four cofactors. The valuation optimum alone does not decide this.
- Can a productive consumer use a factored or streamed relation with a favorable complete physical bill? Specify its endpoint and price arithmetic, passes, precision and restoration; an identity producing zero is not that consumer.

## Related open work

The refreshed open-PR body corpus contains no other result on this fixed generator's sparse-support coefficient valuations. Related broader tensor-interface work is distinct:

- [#7249](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7249) bounds approximate Gaussian tensor-child fusion through rectangular adapters. Its target and norm-error quantities differ; no coefficient-height value is shared.
- [#7172](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7172) studies doubled centre-Gram stabilization and its annihilator. It uses a different operator and computes no shared valuation mass.

The completion refresh read the eight other open account PRs created since the CLAIM: #7247, #7248, #7249, #7251, #7252, #7253, #7254 and #7255. None studies this fixed generator's coefficient-height or split-prime valuation quantity. The broader tensor relationships are recorded above and below; no additional scientific computations checked another result.

- [#7247](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7247) counts contiguous blocks in a rounded tensor image. Its layout quantity differs from coefficient heights; no value is shared.
- [#7252](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7252) determines finite-field multiplication-tensor stabilizer determinant images and orbit counts. Its tensor and arithmetic quantity differ; no valuation value is shared.

Sparse local-note and unpublished-work coverage remains incomplete; the package records the search limits.
